thread.title: Sheldon Whitehouse Buys Tesla Stock, Sells Apple

title: Sheldon Whitehouse Buys Tesla Stock, Sells Apple
text:
Sheldon Whitehouse Buys Tesla Stock, Sells Apple By Jan. 11, 2019 12:32 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images Text size
About a year ago, Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D., R.I.) co-wrote an editorial in The Wall Street Journal, advocating for better roads and bridges.
Whitehouse, who sits on the Environment and Public Works Committee and its Subcommittee on Transportation and Infrastructure, recently saw his family’s investments make some interesting turns near the end of 2018.
The senator disclosed in a regulatory form Thursday that he purchased Tesla stock (ticker: TSLA) in both personal and joint accounts in December. Whitehouse also bought Square stock (SQ), while selling shares of Apple (AAPL), Union Pacific (UNP), and Ford Motor (F), among others.
In response to a request for comment, Whitehouse’s Senate office stated that “trades made in the Senator’s account are conducted independently by a financial advisor without any input from the Senator or his family.”
The senator bought Tesla stock in two transactions, each valued at between $1,001 and $15,000, on Dec. 28. Filers aren’t required to disclose specific amounts for transactions, only ranges. One purchase was for his personal account, and the other was for a joint account that he holds with his wife, Sandra, a “marine biologist and environmental advocate,” according to his site .
Tesla had disclosed that day the addition of Oracle (ORCL) founder Larry Ellison to its board. We noted that Ellison is a “very close” friend of Tesla CEO Elon Musk.
While he was buying Tesla on Dec. 28, Whitehouse was selling Ford stock. He sold from a personal account Ford stock valued at $1,001 to $15,000, and sold an equal amount of the stock from a joint account. Ford shares were pummeled by macro and company-specific challenges in 2018, and ended the year down nearly 39%.
Whitehouse also bought Square stock valued from $1,001 to $15,000 for a personal account on Dec. 28, as the shares closed in on a 62% gain for the year. Days later, in January, the payments company named a new chief financial officer .
The senator had material holdings in Apple, owning a total of between $200,00 and $500,000 of the iPhone maker’s stock in a trust and a joint account as of the end of 2017, according to a filing . Whitehouse had been selling Apple stock that year, and also earlier in 2018 , before a sale on Dec. 4 from his personal account of shares valued between $15,001 and $50,000. Apple stock went on to have a rough December to end a volatile year .
Also on Dec. 4, Whitehouse sold from a personal account Union Pacific stock valued between $15,001 and $50,000. Barron’s noted a slew of upgrades for the railroad earlier this week after it hired a protégé of industry legend Hunter Harrison .
(Editor’s note: This article has been updated to include a comment from Senator Whitehouse’s office.)
